newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP says abnormals blur better result.
newsitem.headline: BHP says abnormals blur better result.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, Australia's largest listed company, said on Friday that its 1996/97 profit result had been blurred by large abnormal losses from writedowns in the major divisions.

"Abnormal items have severely affected results that were otherwise an overall improvement on last year though not at the same level as achieved in 1995," the company said in a statement accompanying its May 31 results.

BHP, which repeated its statement in late May that it had scrapped its 15 percent return-on-equity target for each operation, said it had allocated additional resources to commissioning new projects, but did not elaborate.
It said new targets measured the company against other large companies and some share market indices, but again did not elaborate.

"The targets set require redevelopment initiatives in some areas to ensure consistent progress is made towards achieving acceptable outcomes in all business units, divestment of businesses which will not make satisfactory contributions for

whatever reason, other divestments to maximise value creation, and a concentration of new inititatives on activities that contribute appropriately to the company's shareholder wealth generation targets."
The company said net abnormal losses in 1996/97 rose to A$976 million from A$247 million a year ago, with net profit slumping to A$410 million from A$1.046 billion.
Net profit before abnormal items, however, rose to A$1.386 billion from A$1.293 billion.
